host_note: One workstation: Intel Core i9-13900KF, 125 GiB RAM; BIOS 1836, microcode 0x133, 253 W sustained and short-term limits; 4 x 32 GiB at 4,200 MT/s. Turbo is on. Two faulty performance cores (logical CPUs 8-11) are capped at 2.2 GHz and never used for timing. Every timed run is pinned to the 16 identical efficiency cores, one thread per core, under the shared lock after a quiet-host check. Pinning to identical cores makes the comparisons reproducible. The efficiency cores retain their stock 800 MHz-4.3 GHz range. Absolute seconds from other host settings are not directly comparable; use matched speed-up ratios across settings. These timings are final, not provisional. Final timings on the 16 identical efficiency cores (CPUs 16-31), one thread per core: one on 16, four on 16-19, eight on 16-23, twelve on 16-27, sixteen on 16-31. Each timed command holds the shared lock and starts after two consecutive ten-second quiet samples: one-minute load <=4 and every selected CPU <20% busy. Both samples are retained. Untimed work uses CPUs 0-7 under nice 10. These release timings are final, not provisional.
